ety.text: Verbal derivation from Prakrit चित्त (citta, “mind, psyche”), whence Hindi चित्त (citt), चीत (cīt). Also related to चेतना (cetnā, “to realize, be conscious”).

Hindi verb set चितना (citnā) चीतना (cītnā) Inherited from Prakrit चित्तेइ (cittei, “paints”), from Sanskrit चित्रयति (citráyati, “decorates”), from चित्र (citra, “picture”) + -यति (-yati). Related to Hindi चित्र (citra), चीता (cītā).

s.g: Daliganj (a neighbourhood of Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India)

Etymology tree Sanskrit पेट (peṭa)? Prakrit 𑀧𑁂𑀟 (peḍa) Hindi पेड़ा Inherited from Prakrit 𑀧𑁂𑀟 (peḍa), possibly from Sanskrit पेट (peṭa). Cognate with Punjabi ਪੇੜਾ (peṛā) / پیڑا (peṛā), Gujarati પેંડો (peṇḍo), Marathi पेढा (peḍhā), Odia ପେଡା (peḍā), ପେଣ୍ଡା (peṇḍā), Bengali পেঁড়া (pẽṛa).
